newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU urges members to resume Bosnia envoy contacts.
newsitem.headline: EU urges members to resume Bosnia envoy contacts.

text.p: The European Union presidency urged all 15 EU states on Friday to resume contacts with Bosnian ambassadors after a deal between feuding Moslem, Serb and Croat leaders on the distribution of ambassadorial posts.

It said the international community's High Representative in Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp, recommended that the suspension of contacts be lifted following the accord arranged by U.S. envoy Richard Holbrooke among Bosnia's leaders.
"The presidency is very pleased with this decision and has suggested to its partners to carry out this recommendation," the Luxembourg presidency of the EU said in a brief statement.

Under the deal, the Bosnian envoy to the United Nations would be a Moslem, a Serb would be appointed ambassador to Washington and a Croat would serve as envoy to Japan, Holbrooke and other mediators told reporters.

The United States and European countries froze contacts earlier this week after rival Moslem, Croat and Serb political leaders failed to agree how to divide up 33 diplomatic posts by an August 1 deadline set by major powers.
Bosnia's current ambassadors were appointed by the wartime Moslem-led central government which fought separatist Serbs and, for 10 months, Croat forces, their nominal allies.

Serb and Croat leaders had complained that the Moslems, the largest community, were dominating the diplomatic service. Moslems in turn feared that their rivals would appoint separatists to the posts, undermining Bosnia's statehood.
